Ai2 also publishes fine-tuned OlmoEarth models (the olmoearth_projects configurations and their task cards) that are not in this listing; say so instead of presenting this list as every model the user can run. prediction_type says what a model outputs: a *_regression output is a value per pixel, not a class probability and not a confidence.

text: The KarstBinary 2025 prediction is `dd504793-1ac3-4a1c-a389-707dbaab56c5` (completed). I need to fetch its results in order to obtain the result_id.
The result is a [0,1]-score-like regression layer: `sample_karst_score`. Let's check the declared output range with olmoearth_get_prediction_result.

Since this band is a regression with [0,1] range, we can read it as P(positive) for ranking purposes — no threshold needed. We'll call olmoearth_review_set_from_result with result_id and the default grid (10). We might use budgets like [0.05]. Alright, let's give it a shot.

result.assumption: The band is a score in [0, 1] decided at 0.5 and is treated as P(positive) for ranking only: each window's scores are [1 - s, s], so its margin is |2s - 1| and the least decided windows (s nearest 0.5) are opened first; the most confident windows (s near 0 or 1) come last. Ranking by distance from 0.5 needs no calibration, but these numbers are not probabilities of error, and no recorded experiment grades this case.

sampling.what_a_window_is: a grid of sampled points, not every pixel: the result's extent is cut into 10 x 10 cells and each window is ONE pixel-value sample at its cell centre, so a window stands for its cell only as far as that pixel does
sampling.nodata_rule: a sample is no-data, and is dropped before ranking, when its band is missing or NaN, equals the model's nodata_value, lies outside the band's declared regression range, or carries no class on a classification band

result.signal: margin = distance from the decision (lower = more suspect, opened first); the most confident windows come last, never first

ceiling.note: No ranking can catch more than this share of the errors at a budget; judge a realised capture against it, not against 1.0. Pass error_rate (known or estimated) for the number.

result.listing_note: review lists all 7 windows of the review set at budget 0.1, in review order, so no list file is written; review_set_evidence.json (evidence_detail_path) holds evidence text only, no windows.

margin_summary.reading: Over all 72 windows: lowest_margin is the smallest margin (the most suspect window) and highest_margin the largest; median_margin is the middle value (half the windows lie below it), not a lower end. margin_at_budget_cut is the 7-th lowest margin (n_review at the budget); review_set is the margin range of all 7 windows in the review set, listed or not. The 65 windows not listed (not_listed) have margins from 0.785875 to 0.991517.

result.evidence_scope: The ranking evidence (exp70 of 2imi9/olmoearth_inferenceX) was measured on OlmoEarth models' class-score margins and does not cover this case: no recorded experiment grades a regression score read as a probability.
caveats: Budgets are fractions of the valid sampled windows, not of the map's pixels.
This review set is chosen to hold errors; it is not a sample, and its error rate overstates the map's. To say how wrong the map is, use olmoearth_plan_label_sample.

facts.sentence: The median margin over all 72 windows (0.96469) is 1.30 to 3.25 times the margins of all 7 windows in the review set, every one listed (0.296909 to 0.744685).

must_state: No recorded experiment grades a regression score read as a probability.

forbidden_claims.why: the margin orders windows for review; it is not a probability of error, and the review set is chosen to hold errors, not sampled, so no error rate follows from it without labelling a designed sample (olmoearth_plan_label_sample)

evidence_scope names upstream evidence (exp70) that the tool says does not cover this case: none of its numbers, its dataset or its finding that the margin ranks errors well applies here, neither 'in comparable cases' nor as 'upstream evidence shows'; the file at evidence_detail_path keeps that record, not a finding about this case

result.next_step: To estimate how wrong this map is, pass scores_path to olmoearth_plan_label_sample (it chooses which windows to label); the file also holds each window's location for the reviewer.

content:
I pulled the KarstBinary 2025 result (`419c581d-...`) and ran the review-set ranking. It's a [0, 1] karst-score layer decided at 0.5; 10×10 grid over the AOI gave **72 valid windows** (28 no-data dropped). The tool ranks by margin — distance from the 0.5 decision — so the least-decided windows come first.

**Check these first** (at a 5% budget: rows 1–4; at 10%: all 7):

| Rank | Window (row, col) | Score vs 0.5 | Margin | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #47 (4, 7) | 0.352 (below) | 0.297 | least decided |
| 2 | #42 (4, 2) | 0.285 (below) | 0.431 | near-boundary |
| 3 | #5 (0, 5) | 0.745 (above) | 0.490 | near-boundary |
| 4 | #18 (1, 8) | 0.223 (below) | 0.554 | below cut for 5% budget |
| 5–7 | #85 (8,5), #28 (2,8), #13 (1,3) | 0.808 / 0.167 / 0.872 | 0.615–0.745 | in 10% set only |

Why: these sit closest to the karst/non-karst boundary, where the model is least committed; context-wide margins range 0.297–0.992 (median 0.965), so this set is clearly separated from the confident majority.

Caveats: the score is treated as P(positive) for ranking only — it's not an error probability, and no recorded experiment grades a regression score read this way. This set is designed to hold errors, not sample them, so use `olmoearth_plan_label_sample` with the saved scores file if you want an honest error rate. Say the word and I'll set that up.
